title: MaxName
description: MAXGEN 2.0 -- One MaxName is what is known about one name: its canonical form, its variants and cross-language cognates (each citing evidence and carrying the claim status ladder), and its phonetic keys.

name_id.description: This name record's own id: a random UUID created once by the writer and never reused.

canonical_form.description: The modern standard spelling used as the anchor for every variant (such as the made-up surname Quillfeather), not necessarily English.

canonical_script_as_written.description: The writing system in the writer's own words, given when canonical_script is other.

form.description: The preferred form in this language or region.

language.description: The language this form is preferred in, as an ISO 639 code.

locale.description: A narrower region, as an ISO 3166-2 code.

notes.description: When and where this form is used, and any caveats.

items.description: One preferred form in one language or region.

regional_canonical.description: Preferred forms of the name in other languages or regions, so no one language is the anchor.

name_type.description: What kind of name this is: given, surname, patronymic, matronymic, occupational, topographic, clan, byname, religious, title or other.

name_type_as_written.description: The kind of name in the writer's own words, given when name_type is other.

gender.description: The gender the name is associated with in its own culture (a cultural association, never a statement about any person).

gender_as_written.description: The association in the writer's own words, given when gender is other.

language_of_origin.description: The language the name ultimately comes from, as an ISO 639-3 code.

etymology.description: Where the name comes from and what it meant, written for a general reader.

see_also_urls.description: Addresses of reference works about the name.

variants.description: Every known variant form; each is its own claim with evidence, retracted rather than deleted.

algorithm_version.description: Which Soundex variant produced the code.

soundex.description: Soundex code of the canonical form.

algorithm_version.description: Which NYSIIS version produced the code.

nysiis.description: NYSIIS code of the canonical form.

algorithm_version.description: Which Metaphone version produced the code.

metaphone.description: Metaphone code of the canonical form.

double_metaphone.description: Double Metaphone codes of the canonical form.

values.description: The codes (this algorithm may give several).

daitch_mokotoff.description: Daitch-Mokotoff Soundex codes of the canonical form.

language_set.description: The language set used (any, ashkenazi, sephardic, or a list of languages).

beider_morse.description: Beider-Morse phonetic codes of the canonical form.

phonetic_keys.description: Phonetic codes of the canonical form for fuzzy search, each with the algorithm version that made it so indexes rebuilt later do not mismatch silently.

cognates.description: Related names in other languages; a first pass may name the target only by related_canonical_form and a later linking pass adds related_name_id.

redistribution_license.description: Whether this name record may be shared (unclear means ask, never guess).

variant_id.description: This variant's own permanent id, created once by the writer so the variant can be cited, disputed or retracted on its own.

assertion_id.description: Helper-owned: this variant's claim id, created once when it is first stored and used by apply-proof and retract.

asserted_at.description: Helper-owned: when this variant was first stored.

status.description: Helper-owned: where this variant stands on the claim status ladder (new ones are proposed; only the proof path changes it).

status_reason.description: Helper-owned: why the status last changed.

status_task_id.description: Helper-owned: the task under which the status last changed.

task_id.description: The task that added this variant.

evidence.description: The one piece of evidence for this variant: a record where it appears, or a saved page of a name dictionary (authored, so capped at 0.4).

confidence.description: The writer's confidence in this variant on this evidence, from 0 to 1 (at most 0.4 when the evidence is not reliable).

variant_text.description: The variant exactly as the records give it, keeping capitals, accents and spelling.

variant_type.description: How the variant relates to the canonical form: spelling_variant (same sound, other spelling), nickname, anglicization, gaelicization, latinization, abbreviation (such as Wm for William), diminutive, cognate, scribal_corruption (a clerk's error), phonetic_rendering (spelled by sound), emigration_adaptation, translation, patronymic_form or other.

variant_type_as_written.description: The kind of variant in the writer's own words (or a published vocabulary's address), given when variant_type is other.

locale.description: The region where the variant was used, as an ISO 3166 or ISO 3166-2 code (the more specific the better).

language.description: The language the variant appears in, as an ISO 639 code.

script.description: The writing system of the variant, given when it differs from canonical_script.

script_as_written.description: The writing system in the writer's own words, given when script is other.

transliteration_standard.description: The transliteration standard used, when the variant was carried over from another script.

period_start.description: The earliest year the variant is attested, from a known example; left out when unknown.

period_end.description: The latest year the variant is known in use; left out when it is still used.

frequency.description: How common the variant is in records of its period and place: rare (under 5 percent), occasional (5 to 25), common (25 to 60), dominant (over 60) or other.

frequency_as_written.description: How common it is, in the writer's own words, given when frequency is other.

attestation_source.description: Where the variant is documented, in words (the evidence link is the citation that counts).

notes.description: Anything else about the variant: why it arose, who used it, caveats.

disputed_by.description: Sources that contest the variant; a disputed variant is kept and flagged, never deleted.

variant.description: One variant form of the name, held as a claim: it cites evidence, carries the claim status ladder and is indexed so apply-proof and retract reach it.

dispute_id.description: This dispute's own permanent id, created once by the writer.

disputing_source.description: The source that contests the variant.

task_id.description: The task that recorded this dispute.

dispute.description: One source that contests a variant.

cognate_id.description: This cognate link's own permanent id, created once by the writer.

assertion_id.description: Helper-owned: this cognate link's claim id, created once when it is first stored and used by apply-proof and retract.

asserted_at.description: Helper-owned: when this cognate link was first stored.

status.description: Helper-owned: where this cognate link stands on the claim status ladder (new ones are proposed; only the proof path changes it).

status_reason.description: Helper-owned: why the status last changed.

status_task_id.description: Helper-owned: the task under which the status last changed.

task_id.description: The task that added this cognate link.

evidence.description: The one piece of evidence for this cognate link: a record where it appears, or a saved page of a name dictionary (authored, so capped at 0.4).

confidence.description: The writer's confidence in this cognate link on this evidence, from 0 to 1 (at most 0.4 when the evidence is not reliable).

related_name_id.description: The related MaxName, once it exists; a first-pass link may leave it out and a later linking pass fills it in.

related_canonical_form.description: The related name's canonical form (such as Johann for John): the only name of the target until related_name_id is filled in, and a readable copy after.

relationship_type.description: How the names are related: etymological_root (the related name is the historical ancestor), cross_language_cognate (parallel forms from one root), derivative (this name was formed from the related one), contracted_form or other.

relationship_type_as_written.description: How they are related, in the writer's own words, given when relationship_type is other.

direction.description: The direction seen from this record: this_derives_from, this_is_source_of, parallel_cognate (both from a shared root) or other.

direction_as_written.description: The direction in the writer's own words, given when direction is other.

attestation_source.description: Who says the names are related, in words (the evidence link is the citation that counts).

notes.description: Anything else about the link: its historical path, caveats, regional differences.

cognate.description: One cognate link, held as a claim; it needs related_name_id or related_canonical_form (or both, once resolved).
